rule_findings.rationale: Implemented behavior matches the phase design's pinned interfaces: helper shape and glob semantics (P3-1) in src/state/approval-rules.ts, settlement record plus numeric-aware comparator (P3-4) in src/contracts/durable-state.ts:202-241, the three enumerated settlement routes with prospective-evidence overlay (P3-5) in state.ts/transitions.ts/gates.ts, and dormant consumption (P3-6/P3-7). Material departures discovered during implementation — deferring autonomous consumption to Phase 5, excluding simple revisions, leaving planned_final_phase human-derived, bounded gate-summary truncation — were written back into both governing documents and enumerated, and files touched beyond the design's summary (maintained docs) are disclosed in the impl-notes.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: Phase 3 implementation output against an approved phase design, with parent design.md, phases/3/design.md and new impl-notes.md co-produced (deviation lists: phase design items 13-14; impl-notes 'Deviations from Plan').

rule_findings.rationale: No settlement is consumed as authority here. The only reader anywhere in src is src/state/request-composition.ts:562-567, which appends the persisted trigger match to an ordinary human gate's summary; authority consumers still require authenticated human approval (transitions.ts predicates hasAuthenticatedArtifactApproval/hasAuthenticatedCombinedDesignApproval/hasAuthenticatedMigrationAudit; next-action.ts contains no settlement reference at all; planned-final-phase.ts derives the bound only from an archived 'approve' decision over retained design bytes and refuses to establish one from fresh produce bytes at :112-116). The waiver route appends a settlement but is not treated as approval of produced bytes and additionally re-verifies human-approved upstreams (gates.ts:606-625). Settlements bind task_id, phase_instance, step, subject_digest and revision+1 (approval-rules.ts:222-237) and are selected only when digest-matched and past the latest restart cutoff (restart-authority.ts:43-64). A human-requested simple revision cannot carry a settlement (transitions.ts:261-264) and always returns to the human gate. One stale comment at state.ts:144-147 still calls a settlement 'alternative authority to an approval'; it describes no behavior in this change and grants nothing.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: The change introduces machine-evaluated approval rules (src/state/approval-rules.ts) and durable rule settlements (TaskStateV1.rule_settlements, src/contracts/durable-state.ts:202-241,350) written at final triage (src/mcp/handlers/state.ts:120-185), accepted-editorial produce re-entry (src/state/transitions.ts:240-265), and authenticated policy-waiver discharge (src/state/gates.ts:590-663) — machinery whose eventual purpose is advancing without a human gate.

rule_findings.rationale: Each new path fails closed toward a human instead of reporting success: an unassessable fixed point mints no settlement and the ordinary gate still opens; waiver-path problems surface as explicit issues with named reasons; an accepted material finding cannot be relabelled away by a 'simple' revision. When a large content match exceeds the bounded gate-summary contract, approvalRuleGateSummary (approval-rules.ts:75-86) preserves the trigger, shows exact leading paths, and states how many were omitted and that the complete set remains durable, rather than silently dropping evidence. The impl-notes report concrete suite counts including the pre-rebuild stale-bundle failures.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: New failure/uncertainty paths: settleApprovalRules returns undefined on every failure incl. a catch (src/mcp/handlers/state.ts:128-184), the waiver route issues named STATE_INVALID reasons policy-waiver-settlement-config-unavailable/-upstream-invalid/-fixed-point-invalid (src/state/gates.ts:614-648), and triage stays the fail-closed action while accepted findings remain (src/review/fixed-point.ts:540-544).

rule_findings.rationale: Settlements carry task_id, phase_instance, step and subject_digest derived mechanically from the settling state (approval-rules.ts:222-237) and live only inside that task's state.json — no new cross-task reads or external authority files. Selection requires an exact subject_digest match, the same phase instance, and survival of the latest restart cutoff, so stale or byte-identical-after-restart settlements are ineligible. Zod refinements enforce sorted-unique ordering and reject a settled_at_revision above the current revision (durable-state.ts:676-695); malformed or unreadable config/evidence yields no settlement at all.
rule_findings.trigger_evidence: A new durable record class (RuleSettlementV1) is persisted in task state and later read for gate presentation (src/state/restart-authority.ts:43-64; src/state/request-composition.ts:562-567).
